holidays.name: National Bake Cookies Day
holidays.description: A sweet day for rolling up your sleeves, preheating the oven, and filling the kitchen with the smell of fresh cookies just in time for the holiday rush. Chocolate chip, sugar, gingerbread, and oatmeal raisin all get their moment.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday, popular in the United States, that grew out of the tradition of holiday cookie baking in December. Its exact creator is unknown, and it spread mostly through food blogs and social media.
holidays.funFact: The chocolate chip cookie was invented by accident in the 1930s by Ruth Wakefield at the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts. Her recipe became so popular that it was printed on the Nestlé chocolate chip package.

holidays.name: International Migrants Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that honors the contributions of migrants around the world and calls attention to their rights, safety, and dignity. Communities mark it with cultural events, storytelling, and food festivals.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly proclaimed it in 2000, after adopting the International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families on December 18, 1990.
holidays.funFact: Roughly 1 in 30 people in the world lives outside the country where they were born, which means a lot of the foods, songs, and words you love have traveled.

holidays.name: Arabic Language Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the Arabic language, spoken by hundreds of millions of people, with its flowing calligraphy, rich poetry, and words that have shaped many other languages. Fans celebrate with calligraphy workshops and poetry readings.
holidays.origin: The UN designated it in 2010 to celebrate multilingualism and cultural diversity. December 18 was chosen because it marks the day in 1973 when the UN General Assembly made Arabic an official UN language.
holidays.funFact: English borrowed many everyday words from Arabic, including coffee, sugar, algebra, magazine, and sofa.

holidays.name: Answer the Telephone Like Buddy the Elf Day
holidays.description: A pop culture holiday where you answer every call with the cheerful line from Elf: 'Buddy the Elf, what's your favorite color?' Spreading cheer by phone is the whole point, even if the person on the other end is confused.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, fan-driven celebration inspired by the 2003 Christmas comedy Elf starring Will Ferrell. It circulates on social media and holiday calendars each December.
holidays.funFact: Will Ferrell's Buddy the Elf famously eats spaghetti topped with maple syrup, a combination that fans of the movie try for themselves.

holidays.name: Maple Syrup Day (Unofficial Sticky Celebration)
holidays.description: A day for pouring maple syrup over pancakes, waffles, and anything else that can stand a little stickiness.
holidays.origin: This is an informal food observance promoted by syrup lovers and food calendars. Maple syrup has been made by Indigenous peoples of North America for centuries, long before it became a breakfast staple.
holidays.funFact: It takes about 40 gallons of maple sap to boil down into just 1 gallon of maple syrup.
